dossier.public_summary: The 24% 0.56-day dip is centered on the star itself and shows odd and even eclipses with very different depths, an extreme V shape and a period identical to the star's own spot period. These signs and the stellar size imply a stellar companion or rotation folded as an eclipse, not a planet.

reasons.why: Undiluted dip implies a stellar-sized companion (diameter ~50% of the M dwarf), not a planet.
Odd and even eclipses differ strongly and steadily across 82 transits, classic for a binary folded at 0.557 d vs 1.11 d.
reasons.value: odd_even.diff_sigma 45.99 (depth_odd_ppm 257100 vs depth_even_ppm 177500, depth_difference 0.3097, depth_ratio 1.4) ; sectors.p_constant 1.365e-108

reasons.why: Extremely V-shaped grazing eclipse incompatible with a flat-bottomed planet, even grazing, shape favours stellar eclipse.
Period exactly matches star's spot period and depths scatter wildly at pp_thousand level, as expected if spot modulation contaminates eclipses / folded variability, not a steady transit.
On-target rules out a neighbour blend, so the ~24% dip is on the target M dwarf itself - an eclipsing binary or rotating spotted artefact, not a planet.
